findings.description: The profiling_status rustdoc ends with "None is mapped to `NOT_STARTED` or any other filter automatically." The intended meaning is "none of these response values is mapped", but on a field whose type is `Option<String>` the sentence reads naturally as a statement about `Option::None` — i.e. that leaving the filter unset defaults to NOT_STARTED, the exact opposite of the implemented behavior (targets.rs:79-86 omits the parameter entirely when the option is None, proved by the empty-query assertion at targets.rs:423-427). This is the plan-mandated migration guidance (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:156-159 "Preserve; do not map to NOT_STARTED"), so an ambiguous reading here is the one place it matters.
findings.required_fix: Reword targets.rs:39-40 so the subject is unambiguous, e.g. "No response value is automatically mapped to `NOT_STARTED` or any other filter value, and an unset filter sends no `profiling_status` parameter."

findings.description: The new struct rustdoc ("Invalid values fail before authentication or dispatch, so their validation errors do not carry a dispatched operation name.") closes most of the attempt-02 diagnostic finding but still does not name the observable error kind. Because query() validates skip/limit/search/adapter_uuid/target_type/status/profiling_status in one pass and returns a bare crate::Error::new(crate::ErrorKind::Validation) (targets.rs:83) with no parameter indication and operation() == None, a caller matching on errors from list/list_pages/list_all has no in-crate statement that every refused query value — including an undeclared profiling_status — surfaces as ErrorKind::Validation with no request sent.
findings.required_fix: Name the kind in the struct rustdoc at targets.rs:15-16, e.g. "Any unsupported query value, including an undeclared `profiling_status`, fails as `ErrorKind::Validation` before authentication or dispatch; no request is sent and the error carries no operation name or caller value."

findings.description: The rustdoc restates the four accepted values as a prose literal while the enforced vocabulary is generated from the pinned spec into TARGET_PROFILING_FILTER_VALUES (tools/red_team_management_models.py:241-244 -> crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team_management.rs:360-361). `tools/generate_models.py --check` byte-compares the generated constant, and tools/red_team_management.py:54 hash-pins the vendor component, but nothing binds the doc comment to either, so a reviewed future vocabulary change can leave this doc list stale without any check failing. The same duplication exists in the unit-test literals (targets.rs:408).
findings.required_fix: Either cite the generated source in the doc (e.g. "the vendor `ProfilingStatusFilter` domain of the pinned management 0.86.0 spec, enforced by `TARGET_PROFILING_FILTER_VALUES`") or extend the generator/unit check to assert that the documented list equals TARGET_PROFILING_FILTER_VALUES.

findings.description: In unknown_discriminators_and_required_vertex_types_stay_validated the inner loop iterates Mode::Request, Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults, but for the `{"type":"client_session","future":null}` case the `else if mode != Mode::Request` branch asserts nothing for Mode::Request, so one of six iterations parses a response schema in request mode and silently discards the outcome. Either request-mode behavior for that payload is a contract worth pinning or the mode should not be iterated for that case.
findings.required_fix: Assert the intended Mode::Request outcome explicitly for the client_session case, or restrict the mode list for that payload so no iteration of the loop is unasserted.
